doc.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025

chapter: Career and the business of an unusual instrument
title: Not being 'just jazz', and refusing to chase danceability
summary: He says venues wanting traditional jazz are not for his band; a big band declined to take them out because the music wasn't danceable.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: career, to find all of these places that like understand enough for us to work with them and they are able to show the mutual respect and help promote the show together and you know, so it’s taking a long time.

How about the fact that if you look at your promo and you see – I’ll just read this, “A contemporary jazz fusion album that encompasses everything from funk to bluegrass to blues, to classical Indian music.” Again, is that a plus? I mean you would think it would be but maybe some people, “Well I just want jazz.”

Yeah, okay, so that’s the thing. Listen, if you want jazz then go get that. That’s not what this is. Period. Now if that means that we lose opportunity because this venue wants traditional jazz? Then we’re not playing there, because that’s not a space for us. You see what I’m saying? Which means that like the whole point, like I said from the beginning, the whole point of music, the self-expression thing, it just so happens that my self- expression and the way that my band plays is this amalgamation of all of this stuff. That’s literally what it is. So like if there’s a place or a promoter or something that doesn’t rock with that, then that’s okay. Because that’s not what we’re supposed to be. And it’s taken many years for even me to be just philosophically sound with the fact that that’s how it is. Because there was a time where because these doors were shut to us that affects the livelihood. That affects – like the fewer places you can play and the less options you have the less likely it is that you make a sustainable living. You see what I’m saying?

Now I think for me and my band and the way that we operate it’s way more important for us to just be ourselves than it is for, well if we do this then now these people will like us and now we’re getting into this thing. Then we’re not being genuine. Like there’s a band, where I’m not going to name the names, I’m not going to name the names of this band but it’s a pretty big band and they were like we’d love to take you guys on the road as an opener, like it’s be great to take you guys on the road as an opener, but I see like people don’t really dance to your music like that. Your music’s not danceable. It’s not just like hard headed dance music the whole time, and that was the reason that they decided to not take us on the road. Right? Now there’s two things I can do with that. I can adapt my music to be like this dance hit thing the whole time and now I’ve gained this opportunity. Or I can just be myself and keep getting the most genuine people who actually like what I do. That’s way more fulfilling.
Yeah, I’ll pick door number two.
